description: The Milnor sign line and the Bring-monodromy sign line are isomorphic as S_3-representations but are not the same section: the monodromy sign character factors through S_3 and is constant on pure-braid closures, while mu-bar_123 separates the Borromean rings from the unlink. Also records that the corpus's stated Borromean braid word closes to 2 components, not 3.

computation.arithmetic: exact: permutations of finite sets and reduced free-group words (tuples of ints). No floating point, no numerical anchor, no q dependence.

rows.stated_word: sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_2 in B_4

F1_inventory_braid_words.note: component count is a braid-word invariant needing no convention beyond which generator swaps which strands; both natural readings of the 0-indexing give these counts

F2_borromean_is_a_pure_B3_braid.note: B_3 is the braid group of the colour fibre's monodromy (rem:holonomy-trefoil; bring_cubic_monodromy_probe A6/A7)

F4_separation.right: closure of the trivial braid      =  3-component unlink
F4_separation.mu_bar_123_right: 0     (CITED: the unlink carries no triple invariant)
F4_separation.conclusion: the sign character factors through S_3 and is therefore constant on pure-braid closures; mu-bar is not, so the two are different functions of the configuration

F5_arity_check_and_residual.arity_check: the monodromy sign character is a function of a LOOP; mu-bar is a function of a LINK; F4 compares them only after pulling both back to B_3, which is a genuine common domain
F5_arity_check_and_residual.why_open: the six local monodromies are half-twists, but the existing probe records them as PERMUTATIONS only — their braid lifts are not computed, so the subgroup they generate is unknown
F5_arity_check_and_residual.consequence_if_image_pure_part_is_trivia: the two sections would agree VACUOUSLY on the realised image without being the same function; that would not restore a canonical identification, but it would weaken the practical force of the separation
F5_arity_check_and_residual.next_step: lift the six local monodromies from S_3 to B_3 (each a half-twist about a vanishing cycle) and compute the subgroup

summary.separating_invariant: ker(B_3 -> S_3) = P_3, the pure braid group
summary.scope: (b) structural exclusion of the CANONICAL identification, backed by a named invariant; not an exclusion of the isomorphism, which each route still has on its own side
summary.corrects: dg07 §7.4's 'the two routes are one route with two derivations of its key step' — too strong; same group and same three objects, but different sections
summary.residual: F5 — the separation is unconditional on B_3, but whether this fibration's monodromy image realises a witnessing pair is NOT established: the local monodromies are recorded as permutations, not braid lifts
does_not_touch: statement B (2026-08-30 Brunnian isotype exclusion) — runs entirely on the Milnor side
B-i (Alt^3 is a non-trivial line) — a fact about the monodromy alone
summary.corpus_defect_flagged: binding-knots-visual-inventory states the Borromean braid word as sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_2 sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_2 in B_4, whose closure has 2 components; two further rows in the same table also miss their component count
